A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Tra-MoE study and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and Appendix A.1–A.5. The relocated supplementary material supports a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LIBERO and real-world robot experiments, ablations, repeated evaluations, and trajectory prediction errors in Tables 1–5 and Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a quantitative comparison of trajectory error and downstream policy success in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The Top-1 sparse MoE architecture, adaptive trajectory masks, frozen trajectory model during policy training, and training objectives remain unchanged. Figure 3 clarifies an already-described procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LIBERO suites, 92 RLbench training tasks, and five real-world manipulation tasks with robot demonstrations and human videos. The added cross-embodiment and physics-engine wording clarifies existing coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain ATM/Tra-baseline, its width- and depth-expanded variants, and the hand-drawn-mask alternative. Figure 5 compares configurations already represented in the existing experiments.

E3.justification: Reported data counts, training budgets, model configurations, MSE and success-rate metrics, and 20-trial-per-task evaluations are retained. Figure 5 analyzes existing configurations; newly listed clipping and warm-up settings do not establish a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds Figure 5, examining the relationship between validation MSE and policy success across five configurations. This extends v1's two reported MSE values and qualitative examples. Existing ablation questions and trajectory visualizations remain.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 and Table 5 retain the same three-run reporting, individual results, and mean-plus-standard-deviation summaries. The new plot introduces no uncertainty estimates or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Table 3's adaptive-mask scores change from 72.5/74.0/86.0/34.5/66.8 to 69.5/77.0/88.0/30.5/66.3 for Spatial/Goal/Object/Long/average. Figure 5 adds MSE values for three LIBERO-only configurations. Tables 1, 2, 4, and 5 and the mixed-data MSE values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, gating definitions, and loss equations (1)–(9) are unchanged. No new assumptions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims about sparse MoE learning from multiple domains, outperforming expanded dense models, and adaptive policy conditioning. Added examples clarify the existing scope.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, trajectory-quality/policy-success interpretation, and Appendix A.1 limitations are retained. The claim that adaptive masks improve every suite also remains, despite the revised Table 3 no longer supporting it.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project repository link and discloses trajectory-model gradient clipping of 10, policy gradient clipping of 100, and policy warm-up of 0 in Tables 6–7. It also names the simulation engines. These are documentation additions rather than demonstrated implementation changes.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work add citations including AgiBot World, RoboMIND, FLIP, and Latent Action Pretraining. These update the surrounding literature while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording clarifications, updates author and contact information, and adds acknowledgements. The appendix moves after the references under a supplementary-material heading; the main narrative remains largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 5, clarifies labels and captions in Figures 1 and 3, resizes Figure 4, and groups supplementary Tables 5–7 together. The existing trajectory visualization becomes Figure 6, and supplementary displays no longer interrupt the references.

improvement.justification: The added training details, repository information, clearer supplementary organization, and quantitative relationship plot modestly improve reproducibility and presentation. These gains are partly offset by an unresolved inconsistency: the retained all-suite improvement claim conflicts with Table 3's adaptive-mask Long score of 30.5 versus 33.5 for the hand-drawn mask. The core method and most evidence remain unchanged.
